Grout Calculator

Grout calculator: tile size, joint width and depth to grout volume and pounds needed for your floor or wall.

Grout formula

Grout fills the joints around each tile. Volume per square foot = 144 × (L + W) ÷ (L × W) × joint width × joint depth, in inches. Multiply by area, then by grout density—cement grout is roughly 0.058 lb per cubic inch (about 1.6 g/cm³). Manufacturers publish their own coverage charts; use them when available.

Example: 100 sq ft of 12 × 12 in tile, 1/8 in joints, 3/8 in deep: 14,400 × 24/144 × 0.125 × 0.375 = 112.5 cu in ≈ 6.5 lb.

Sanded or unsanded?

  • Unsanded: joints narrower than about 1/8 in, and easily scratched surfaces like polished marble
  • Sanded: joints about 1/8 in and wider
  • Epoxy: showers and kitchens where stain resistance matters

Small tiles have far more joint length—mosaics can need several times more grout than large-format tile.
